slides.statement: A MODEL IS NOT A FEATURE. THE CODE AROUND IT IS.

slides.heading: TWO PLACES
slides.body: AI shows up in your work in two places, and people mix them up. One question tells them apart: if the API key is switched off tomorrow, does the product stop, or do you just type more?
items: The service calls a model at runtime
It runs on every user file, every day
The company pays for as long as it lives
Switch the key off and the product stops
You call a model while you build
You pay once, and only for your own work
Nothing in production depends on it
Switch the key off and you just type more

slides.kicker: When a task earns a harness
slides.statement: IT REPEATS, AND GETTING IT WRONG IS EXPENSIVE.

slides.heading: A harness does four things
blocks: The loop
Call the model again, or stop. And when to stop by force.
Tools
What the model may ask for. It never acts, it asks.
State
What the model sees this turn, and what to drop.
Verification
Code inspects the result before accepting it.

slides.heading: THE CHECK
slides.body: The last trip crosses midnight. The model copies 00:05 from the timetable: well formed, plausible, wrong. Five lines of ordinary Python notice and send it back.
slides.code:
model  23:40, 23:47, 00:05
code   rejected
       23:47 is before 00:05
model  23:40, 23:47, 24:05
code   accepted

slides.statement: THE CHECK COSTS NOTHING. BEING WRONG COSTS MONEY.

slides.heading: TOOL CALL
slides.body: The model executes nothing, it asks. Running the function is the only place your code acts, and it is where the security boundary and the spending control live.
items: You send the messages and the tool definitions
The model replies with stop_reason = tool_use
Your code runs the function and appends tool_result
You repeat until stop_reason is end_turn

slides.heading: Four of them arrive in silence
blocks: max_tokens
Your own limit fired. The answer is cut mid-sentence.
pause_turn
The server loop asks to continue. Do not add «Continue».
refusal
A safety refusal. Only here is stop_details filled in.
context window
The conversation no longer fits and nothing warns you.

slides.heading: THE MESSAGES
slides.code:
+ [0] user       question
+ [1] assistant  tool_use
+ [2] user       tool_result
+ [3] assistant  00:05
+ [4] user       rejected
+ [5] assistant  24:05

slides.heading: WHAT IT COSTS
slides.body: Prices here are Opus 5, as an example. Output costs five times input, and the whole list above is resent every round: 425 input tokens, then 593, then 1247, for one question that never changed.

slides.heading: THE LEVERS
slides.body: A harness can pick a model per sub-task, and full delegation cannot. Every number here was measured on a real run, not taken from an article.
groups: Three levers you own, and one you do not
items: A cheaper model for the mechanical sub-task
Prompt caching: 27 percent off a measured run
Batch processing: asynchronous costs half
How many rounds it takes is the model's decision

slides.statement: PUT A DATE AT THE TOP AND THE CACHE NEVER HITS.

slides.heading: Decisions move from model to code
blocks: You know no rules
Model. Expensive and unpredictable, but it works today.
You see a pattern
In transit. Twenty examples in, a rule shows through.
The rule is in code
Code. Cheap, instant, the same answer every time.
A human at runtime
Someone presses confirm. Deliberately not automated.

slides.heading: RAG
slides.body: Not a separate architecture. Replace read_timetable with search and you have RAG. The weak link is retrieval, not generation.
items: Index: cut documents into chunks
Search: pull chunks for this question
Answer: chunks plus the question go to the model
Search is a tool like any other
If the chunk is missing, the model answers anyway
The model decides how many searches to run
Two questions, two and four searches, measured
Grounding is checked in code, not requested

slides.heading: THE RAG CHECK
slides.body: An honest «not in the sources» is not the default. It happened only because the output shape allowed null and the code refused any citation that was never retrieved.

slides.heading: Decide four things before you code
blocks: The task
One sentence, narrow enough to finish today.
The tools
What the model is allowed to ask for.
The check
What code verifies, in five lines.
When it stops
How many retries, and who gets it then.

slides.heading: THE FILTER
slides.body: Four kinds of check: something must exist, numbers must match, code must run, and the model's own answer goes back through the check. Yours should be one of them.
groups: Filter your idea in this order
items: Triage a ticket: the component must exist
Weekly digest: every number must match code
Bug report into a test: red, then green
Stale comments: the name must be in the code
Can code check the result without a human
Does the task repeat
Does the check fit in five lines
If not, it is a prompt with extra steps
